summary: The hypothesis was confirmed: grid-based nearest-neighbor construction with candidate-list 2-opt consistently scores ~78.43 out of 100, well above the x-sorted baseline. The "carrot constraint" penalty accounts for only ~1% of tour cost and is not the primary optimization lever. Advanced search methods (simulated annealing, iterated local search) proved unstable and did not reliably improve over the deterministic approach.
key_points: Score achieved: 78.43/100, stable across 4 independent runs (78.428, 78.428, 78.428, 78.4275), confirming prediction of ≥78.
Construction quality dominates: pure grid NN scores 78.19; adding penalty-aware 2-opt gains only ~0.24 points, confirming the penalty is a ~1% effect on total tour cost.
SA and ILS variants scored in the 73–78.5 range with high variance due to timing sensitivity under the 2-second time limit — the deterministic greedy approach is more reliable.
Remaining ~21.6 points of improvement likely require fundamentally better TSP algorithms (e.g., LKH-style moves, Or-opt, 3-opt) or more sophisticated tour construction, not penalty optimization.
Next iteration should investigate Or-opt moves, 3-opt, or Lin-Kernighan style perturbations within the time budget to push beyond the 78.4 plateau.
